clue.text: Hiding obsession about spots on skin

indicators.note: about means the word for obsession goes around the spots, enclosing them

parts.note: a thing, as in 'she has a thing about cats', is an obsession
a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on their acne tries to keep it covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' is not concealment here but a beating, as in 'gave him a good hiding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a severe beating, the same as a flogging.

clue.text: Pigs will, in a word, make rubbish

definitions.meaning: with the space moved, pig swill: food slops fed to hogs

explanation.walkthrough: 'in a word' tells you to run 'Pigs will' together and split it as pig swill.
explanation.definitionFit: The term originally meant kitchen slops fed to swine, and now means nonsense.

clue.text: The last cricketer on earth possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the two words could be jumbled into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Musing on who might be the final batsman alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A N Other' is the stand-in name on a British team sheet for an unnamed player, typically the last one picked.
explanation.definitionFit: A. N. Other is the placeholder name for a team's unnamed final player.

clue.text: Rod not required for this tackle?

definitions.text: Rod not required for this tackle?

parts.words: Rod not required for this tackle?
parts.note: fishing gear where the line is held and worked by hand, with no rod

explanation.definitionFit: A fishing line held directly in the fingers needs no rod.

clue.text: Georgia with folk-wisdom in abundance

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
lore is traditional knowledge passed down

explanation.surface: Georgia overflowing with traditional sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore follows a noun to mean plenty of it, in great numbers.

clue.text: Ganymede as holder of trophy

definitions.meaning: the Trojan youth who served wine to Zeus

explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede poured wine for the gods; literally, one bearing a cup is a winner holding silverware.

clue.text: Twist of tobacco marking Napoleon's end?

definitions.meaning: tobacco twisted into a thin rope
Napoleon is the pig in Orwell's Animal Farm, so his rear end

explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is the ruling pig in Orwell's Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco was sold twisted into a braid, and a pig's rear is its curly appendage.

clue.text: Jason the dog?

parts.note: Jason fetched back the Golden Fleece, so he is a dog breed that fetches game

explanation.definitionFit: A gundog breed trained to bring back shot game, as Jason brought back the Fleece.

clue.text: Scolding in a university with bad vibes

indicators.note: bad tells us the letters that follow are spoiled and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry telling-off delivered on campus amid a hostile atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scolding' is the definition; 'bad' is the anagram signal, and 'in' and 'with' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Scolding words are insulting and harsh, i.e. verbally offensive.

clue.text: Silver ring stuck in the sand

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a ring is a round shape, a circle

explanation.surface: A silver ring has been lost on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stuck on a sandbank or shore has run ashore and cannot float off.

clue.text: Gold piece, sovereign, that continues to go round the world

definitions.text: that continues to go round the world

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a piece of something
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: A gold sovereign coin passes from hand to hand around the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests the gold coin, but it gives ER, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite or spacecraft in orbit keeps circling the planet.

clue.text: Cut, more traditional feature of the Oval

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut
older means more old-fashioned, more traditional

explanation.surface: A cut that sounds like a nostalgic feature of a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, long overlooked by large Victorian gas storage tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The huge gas-storage tanks beside the Oval ground are a famous landmark there.

clue.text: Wax general falling to pieces

indicators.note: falling to pieces shows the word general breaks apart and is reassembled

explanation.surface: A wax model of a general is crumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wax' is not candle wax but the verb, as the moon waxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is to grow larger, as the moon does.

clue.text: Film, for example, kept in home

indicators.note: kept in means the example abbreviation is held within the word for home

parts.note: native, as in one's native land, means home
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A roll of film, say, is stored in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A developed photographic film shows tones reversed, the original from which prints are made.

clue.text: Daily functioning as ferryman

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaning lady who comes in each day
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A newspaper serves as a boat operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; in Britain a daily is also a cleaner, a charwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this figure rowed the dead across the Styx to the underworld.

clue.text: Car halted in Salisbury, for example

annotationWithheld.why: Car halted in Salisbury, for example: CAR HALTED is an anagram of the answer but no clue word signals the anagram; an indicator seems lost in the OCR and no search gives the printed clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Car halted in Salisbury, for example

clue.text: Thing one takes on in counter-argument

parts.note: an object is a thing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something a person takes up in a rebuttal.
explanation.definitionFit: An objection is a protest or reason raised against a proposal.

clue.text: See Cuba resort in that?

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Invitation to visit Cuba's holiday resort, for reasons given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but means re-sort: SEE CUBA rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjunctions giving a reason: 'I left in that I was tired'.

clue.text: Annual incomes of girl stars?

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: What a woman's horoscope says about her yearly pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaries are fixed yearly pay for employees.

clue.text: Beat St Paul, perhaps, to first of epistles

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the saint's name could be rearranged differently
first of takes only the opening letter of epistles

explanation.surface: Defeating St Paul in a race to write the first letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns ST PAUL into PULSAT, then E from 'epistles'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulsate is to throb rhythmically, like a heartbeat.

clue.text: One gives reasons for seeing some of the Camargue region

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A debater makes a case for visiting part of the French Camargue.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for seeing' into the definition; 'One gives reasons' is the whole definition and 'for seeing' only links it to the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues puts forward reasons for a position.

clue.text: Gravity-states of conduits?

parts.note: g is the symbol for the acceleration due to gravity
utters means says, states

explanation.surface: A question about how gravity governs water channels.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutters are channels carrying rainwater away from roofs and roads.

clue.text: Ugly thing, a stye!

definitions.meaning: a stye is an inflamed spot on the eyelid, literally a sore eye

explanation.definitionFit: An unsightly object offends the view; read literally, a stye is a painful spot on the eyelid.

clue.text: Blenheim?

parts.note: Blenheim is a grand Oxfordshire palace (a house) and also a red-and-white spaniel kept as a pet, so the name fits both halves

explanation.surface: A one-word clue naming the famous palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Blenheim Palace is the Churchill family seat; a Blenheim is also a toy spaniel variety, a pet kept indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A Blenheim spaniel is a pet kept in the home, and the name also suggests a stately house.

clue.text: Work attitude to resist

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
a pose is a bodily attitude or stance

explanation.surface: Taking a stance at work in order to resist.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose is to stand against something.

clue.text: Shots of Palestein?

indicators.note: shot can mean broken or ruined, so shots of a word are its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about goal attempts by a Palestinian side.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Shots' both as the kicks in football and as wrecked versions of the name, whose letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Penalty kicks are shots at goal awarded for fouls.

clue.text: Computer kept, at first, in unusual depots

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the shuffled warehouse word
unusual signals the letters of depots are arranged in an odd new way
at first takes only the opening letter of kept

explanation.surface: A machine stored in some odd warehouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns DEPOTS into DESTOP, and K (first of 'kept') goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is a personal computer that sits on a desk rather than being carried.

clue.text: Banking flap! No lire exchanged after first of April!

indicators.note: after places the rearranged currency letters behind the April letter
first of takes only the opening letter of April
exchanged, as with money, tells us the letters are swapped around

explanation.surface: No Italian lire could be changed once April began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' is not finance but an aircraft tilting in a turn; 'exchanged' suits the currency surface while signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: This hinged wing surface tilts a plane into a bank.

clue.text: Behaviour in lawsuits

definitions.meaning: deeds or conduct, what someone does

explanation.definitionFit: Deeds make up conduct, and in law the same word names court cases.

clue.text: Energy secure? Check the biological community!

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
cosy means snug and safe, secure
to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: Instructions about energy saving and checking a living environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecologists use the term for interacting organisms and their surroundings as a unit.
